name: Model-driven sports taking (pre-game and hold-to-settlement)
one_line: Take stale in-play quotes off a faster event feed, or scale into model-mispriced lines and hold to settlement; the two styles behind the largest sports accounts.
scope: Cover ONLY the modelling variant: pre-game and in-game directional positions from ratings / Elo / closing-line-value models, sized and held to settlement; leaderboard sports wallets and their PnL, sharp-book lines as benchmark, bankroll and variance, the sports taker fee (0.05 since 2026-07-10, was 0.03: check evidence pack E1) and the cut in sports maker rebates, capacity. Boundary: feed-latency taking is sports-inplay-feed-latency-taking; quoting is sportsbook-anchored-sports-mm.
sub_variants: live score / stadium-feed sniping in football and US sports
merged_from: onchain-bots: Live-data latency taking in esports and in-play sports
adjacent-transfer: In-play data-feed latency, or courtsiding by API
traders: Model-driven sports taker that scales in and holds to settlement
flags: Courtsiding and out-of-licence use of official data breach venue/data-provider terms; possible surveillance attention on the CFTC-regulated US venue; not prohibited by Polymarket international itself.

key_evidence.note: Teardown and failed copy attempt 1 s late ($150 to $138); mechanism claim unverified
KCH123: $743K in 33 days, 10.7K buys / zero sells, NBA vs NHL ROI split
Esports bot ~$230k in five months, $200-$20,000 per bet
Victim-side confirmation: seeing the play first is worth ~40c of EV
Sports marketable orders wait out a delay and cannot be cancelled

parent_scope: Cover two taker styles. (1) Feed latency: official/scout/game-API data vs 15-60 s broadcast delay, esports parsing bots (TeemuTeemuTeemu ~$230k), swisstony scale (hard data) vs claimed mechanism (unverified), size limits from resting depth, per-market secondsDelay, taker delay removals (World Cup), copy-failure proof that the edge lives in the first second. (2) Model-driven: KCH123 probe-wait-slam execution, zero sells, sport-specific ROI (NBA +72.9% vs NHL +0.6%), variance and bankroll, CLV-vs-Pinnacle validation. Include fee 0.05 at mid prices and taker-rebate effect. Boundary: maker-side use of the same feeds is sportsbook-anchored-sports-mm / event-market-making; in-play drift, panic-fade and final-minutes ideas are speculative band; copying these wallets is screened-copy-trading.
critic_notes: SPLIT sports-automated-takers into (a) in-play feed-latency taking and (b) model-driven pre-game / hold-to-settlement taking. They differ in edge (speed and data licence vs model), build (low-latency infrastructure vs modelling and bankroll) and risk (data-terms / surveillance vs variance). E4's Leo Labs reconstruction classes 14 of 18 top sports wallets as directional buy-and-hold, so the evidence base of (a) is one esports bot plus X-thread mechanism claims. Add to (b) a sub-variant the list lacks: systematic underdog buying. arXiv 2609.12878 finds no favourite-longshot bias in sports (longshots +2.4% equal-weighted, +18.1% pooled, pre-fee sample) and The Oracle reports RN1 at 53% of trades under 50c and swisstony at 60%+ of entries under 50c.

sports-automated-takers: 'Established' is supported for directional / model-driven holding (leaderboard PnL), not for in-play feed latency, whose flagship mechanism is unverified and contradicted by E4's wallet reconstruction. Label the sub-variants separately.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: In-play sports latency trading (event data faster than the book)
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Take stale in-play prices in the seconds after goals/scores using a data feed that beats broadcast and other traders.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: A bot subscribes to a low-latency live event feed and lifts resting orders on the now-favoured side before makers reprice. Community teardowns attribute this to swisstony (90% football, ~96k trades at the time, ~$156 average profit per trade); the mechanism attribution is unverified, but the account's scale is hard data. The sports MM interview independently confirms the same asymmetry from the victim side. Position sizes are many small-to-mid clips (typically $10-15k) because in-play depth is limited.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Seconds of latency advantage on a discrete, price-jumping event; TV viewers are 15-40 s behind (claim from Reddit teardown).
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Requires licensed/fast data and execution infra most participants lack; makers who cannot pull in time fund it.
raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Data-rights cost and legality, makers adding event-driven pulls, sports taker fee 0.05 at mid prices, any future sports taker delay (unverified whether one applies), capacity limited by in-play depth. A copy-trader 1 s behind lost money (85 trades, $150 -> $138), showing the edge is entirely in the first second.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Record Polymarket in-play book updates for a weekend of football with timestamps and compare to a commercial live-score API timestamp; measure how long stale quotes survive after a goal and how much size is available.
raw_discovery_candidates.flags: Courtsiding-style or unlicensed data use can breach venue/data-provider terms; on the CFTC-regulated US venue this may attract surveillance attention.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Live-data latency taking in esports and in-play sports
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: React to in-game events (kills, objectives, points, breaks) from a faster data path than the Polymarket book.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: The bot ingests live game state (official game-data feeds, parsed streams, live-score APIs, reportedly over-the-air TV antennas to beat streaming delay) and recomputes win probability on each event. It takes stale quotes before makers reprice, in sizes of $200-$20,000, mostly in Dota 2, LoL and Counter-Strike, with similar tooling appearing for tennis. NBA data shows mispricings cluster in the final minutes of games, which is where this edge concentrates. Maker programs now require quotes to rest 3.5 s to earn rewards, which keeps stale quotes exposed.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Seconds-level information latency between the venue of the event and the order book; thin maker coverage in esports.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: A named wallet demonstrably did it for five months; sportsbook-style in-play delays are absent on the CLOB, so the fastest data path wins.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Data-feed licensing/ToS; match-fixing and delay-abuse scrutiny in esports; makers widening in-play; sports fee 0.05 at mid prices; league partnerships (MLB, May 2026) may bring integrity rules and delays.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: In-play data-feed latency, or courtsiding by API: official and venue feeds against broadcast-delayed counterparties
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Trade live sports and esports markets off data feeds that run 8-45 seconds ahead of the TV or stream that retail watches.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Subscribe to low-latency official data, such as league feeds, scout data, or esports game APIs like Riot and OpenDota. Map scoring and state events to a win-probability jump. Lift stale resting orders, or pull and replace your own quotes, before broadcast viewers react. Broadcast delay is reported at 15-40 s for TV and 30-60 s for streams. Esports tournament streams are deliberately delayed by minutes according to one X post, though official APIs can also be delayed. Polymarket's countermeasure is a configurable in-game taker delay, which protects makers who are also on fast feeds.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: The information arrives seconds ahead of most counterparties. The remaining resting liquidity comes from slower makers and retail limit orders.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Polymarket's live liquidity partly comes from retail and slower makers. Sportsbooks suspend their markets on key events, and an order book does not. Reported wallet PnLs are large. Treat the claimed mechanisms as unverified.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Official feeds are expensive and licence-restricted. A taker delay lets makers on the same feed pull quotes first. Where the delay is removed, you race other feed-holders. Size is limited to the stale resting liquidity. The PnL stories all come from X posts.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Record the Polymarket book against timestamped play-by-play for 20 matches. One collector repo already covers NBA, NHL, Dota and CS2. Measure how many cents of stale liquidity could be taken per event after the configured delay.
raw_discovery_candidates.flags: In-venue courtsiding breaches ticket terms and has led to ejections and bans in tennis. Reselling or scraping official data can breach its licence. It is not prohibited by Polymarket itself. Several jurisdictions geo-block Polymarket (France, Spain, Netherlands in 2026).

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Model-driven sports taker that scales in and holds to settlement ('probe-wait-slam')
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Automated sports model buys mispriced spreads/moneylines in many small probes then large clips, never sells, redeems at settlement.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: A pre-game/in-game sports model produces a fair price; the execution layer probes with tiny fills (median ~$6.67), waits, then takes size (single fills up to ~$190k) when liquidity appears, e.g. 119 fills at exactly $0.50 over 192 minutes on one NBA spread. No exits: every position rides to resolution, so variance is absorbed by bankroll (one NHL game cost $143k). A smaller practitioner reports the same idea in live less-popular sports with Kelly-fraction sizing.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: A better sports model than the Polymarket crowd/makers, plus patient execution that does not move the book.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Polymarket sports lines are partly set by retail flow and thinly staffed makers; NBA spreads/totals and minor sports are softer than sharp books.
raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Sport-specific: the dissected account made +72.9% ROI in NBA but only +0.6% on $3.48M in NHL; averaging down into losers; taker fees at mid prices; model decay; large bankroll needed.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Backtest an existing public sports model (or closing sharp lines as the 'model') against Polymarket prices at T-60/T-10 minutes for a season; measure CLV vs Pinnacle close net of 0.05 fee.
